newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Boto ends debut 20 percent higher.
newsitem.headline: HK's Boto ends debut 20 percent higher.

text.p: Shares of artificial Christmas tree maker Boto International Holdings Ltd soared on Monday to end their trading debut up 20.3 percent compared with their issue price.
The stock rose HK$0.26 to close at HK$1.54 after moving in a range of HK$1.40 to HK$1.68. It was issued at HK$1.28.
Volume was 57.29 million shares worth HK$90.88 million.
"It was much better than we expected," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment.
Brokers said the recent strong debut of Shum Yip Investment Ltd helped boost sentiment surrounding initial public offerings and had given investors a taste for quick profits.
Shares of the Shenzhen-municipal government backed Shum Yip soared 144.6 percent to close their market debut at HK$4.525 on Friday.
Boto makes Christmas related products, including artificial Christmas trees, plastic ornanments, garlands and other decorations.
It issued 125.4 million new shares in a Hong Kong IPO which was 12.6 times subscribed.

"As one of the major local artificial Christmas tree makers, its future prospects are expected to be encouraging due to steady earnings growth," Ng said. "We expect much stronger earnings growth if it can open up more markets in the future."
Boto said net proceeds would be used to set up new manufacturing plants, repay bank borrowings and for general working capital.
The group's principal markets are the United States and Europe.
